observation_summary: The method NumberUtils.createNumber throws a StringIndexOutOfBoundsException when processing strings with invalid exponent positioning (e.g., '1eE'), instead of throwing a NumberFormatException.
reasoning_summary: The fix involves adding conditional checks (guards) to validate the position of the exponent indicator ('expPos') relative to the string length before performing substring operations. Since the root cause is the absence of a validation check for the input string's structure, this is a classic 'Checking' defect.
evidence_used: NumberUtils createNumber throws a StringIndexOutOfBoundsException instead of NumberFormatException when a String containing both possible exponent indicators is passed in.
The fix adds 'if (expPos > str.length())' checks to validate the input before calling substring.

alternative_types.why_not_primary: While the logic for parsing numbers is procedural, the specific failure is a missing boundary check on the input string index, which is the definition of a Checking defect.
